title: Latency signal fabric: p95/p99 per endpoint/model/zone and drift-detection dashboards
creator: Anika Rao
description: Add a unified latency signal layer ('signal fabric') that emits p50/p95/p99 histograms and derived metrics grouped by endpoint (route), model (model-id + quantization variant), and zone (region/availability zone). Build a set of dashboards and automated regression detectors that highlight significant percentile drift and tokens/sec regressions across traffic slices. This work ties telemetry, dashboarding, and alerts together so on-call and SRE can quickly root-cause model/route/zone performance regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry: per-request signals include timing buckets required to compute p50/p95/p99 and token-rate; telemetry must include tags: route, model_id, model_variant, zone, instance_type, batch_size

Aggregation: pipeline produces daily and rolling-1h p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec for every (route, model_id, zone) tuple with retention of 30 days for metrics and 90 days for raw histograms in cold storage
Dashboards: New 'Latency Signal Fabric' dashboards that let engineers pivot by route/model/zone, compare baseline vs current, and show history heatmap and sparklines
Regression detection: Automated detector flags increases in p95 or p99 > 20% over baseline for >10 minutes and posts incidents to the SRE channel with attribution hints
Alerting: Must have noisy-reduction (aggregation + MAB) and runbook links; false-positive rate < 5% on synthetic tests
Backfill: Backfill last 14 days of quantile estimates for most trafficked endpoints for continuity
Documentation: Confluence runbook, schema spec, and console widget docs published
Performance: Telemetry overhead < 3% CPU and < 1% p99 added latency on tail for typical requests
implementation_plan: Instrument: add histogram timing and token counters in inference gateway (authored in gateway/telemetry.ts) — include dimension tags for route/model/variant/zone
Aggregation: extend quantile-rollup service to accept histograms and emit p50/p95/p99 via existing metrics pipeline (Prometheus -> ClickHouse/TSDB)
Storage: ensure histograms are stored in cold storage for forensic playback (S3 bucket prefix s3://redwind-telemetry/histograms/)
Dashboards: create Grafana dashboard templates and console embedded widgets (grafana/dashboard-id: 1429, console-widget: latency-signal-fabric)
Detectors: add a cloud-run job for regression detection using EWMA + bootstrap baseline (configurable window) and wire to PagerDuty + slack channel #sre-latency-alerts
Backfill: run nightly backfill job for 14 days to populate historical baselines
QA: synthetic workload run and canary roll: run synthetic profiles against dev/staging for 72 hours and validate alerts
telemetry_schema: labels: route (string), model_id (string), model_variant (string), zone (string), instance_type (string), batch_size (int), request_size_tokens (int)
histogram_buckets: power-of-two up to 32s with fine-grained tail buckets (e.g., 1ms,2ms,4ms,...,32768ms)
export_frequency: raw histograms every request (low-sample) and 1s aggregated counters to TSDB
alerting_rules: Rule A: p95(route,model,zone) > baseline_p95 * 1.20 for 10m -> severity: P1 -> channel: #sre-latency-alerts + PagerDuty
Rule B: p99(route,model,zone) absolute > 2s for 5m -> severity: P0 -> immediate PD
Rule C: tokens_per_sec drop > 30% for 15m for any model in Dedicated -> severity: P2 -> slack notify ops
Noise-mitigation: require min-traffic threshold (100 reqs/min) and aggregate over 3m windows before firing
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev/staging): instrument gateway and run telemetry pipeline internally; validate schema and end-to-end latency (target: 72h)
Phase 2 (canary): enable for 10% of production routes with read-only dashboards and detectors in alert-only mode (monitor FP rate) for 7 days
Phase 3 (gradual): shift to 50% then 100% with detectors enabled; enable runbook auto-creation on PD triggers
Rollback: revert gateway instrumentation and aggregation flags via feature flag 'latency-sf-enabled' if any production impact > medium
qa_plan: Run inferbench scenarios (short prompt, long prompt, streaming) with synthetic tokens/sec sweeps
Inject latency faults in staging (chaos): add 50-300ms tail noise and confirm detectors fire at expected thresholds
Check dashboard pivots for route/model/zone and validate historical backfill data aligns with pre-existing telemetry
Verify end-to-end instrumentation overhead under 3% using perfbench harness
notes: Decision: use histogram-based quantile estimation (t-digest) in the aggregation service rather than approximate Prometheus histograms to preserve tail fidelity
Trade-off: storing raw histograms increases storage by ~12% but enables accurate reconstructions and postmortem analysis
Opportunity: these signals can later feed Optimize to recommend per-model batching/quantization changes when p99 regressions correlate with sequence length
Related: ties into A/B rollback automation in console for model variant fallback (see product PRD: confluence link above)
